properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/16/2021 to GEOPETRO LLC in Worth Twp, Butler county. OGA3216(A) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to restore disturbed land surface of a well site.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: GEOPETRO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/16/2021
Violation Code: OGA3216(A) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - GENERAL RULE - Failure to restore disturbed land surface of a well site.
Violation ID: 926900
Permit API: 019-21947
Unconventional: Yes
County: Butler
Municipality: Worth Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/16/2021
Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an on-site routine complete inspect, and to summarize the overall status of this well and well location. The project was recently acquired by Big Dog Energy, LLC. Applications for the transfer of all three wells permitted on the site, from Geopetro LLC to Big Dog Energy LLC, were received by the Department on August 2, 2021. An application for the transfer of the ESCGP that is currently active on the site was also received by the Department. The current Operator information has not yet been updated in the Department's electronic database. Well number 019-21947, along with two other wells, (API ID#'s: 019-21948, 019-21927), were drilled and currently exist on the location. Although the Act Nine sign has been changed to reflect the current owner of the well location, the well tags have not yet been updated. Updated well tags should be installed on each of the wells at some point in the near future. Inspection ID number's 2092885, 2092888, and 2092893 (conducted on August 17, 2012) suggests that all of the wells have been stimulated. Subsequent inspections have indicated that the wells have been on inactive status since at least December of 2013. ESCGP number ESX11-019-0109 is currently active on the site. The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 08/07/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. Up until very recently, the property owner had been grazing cattle on the site and using the tank pad as a feedlot. A small sediment slide had developed on the cut bank surface to the east of the well location. With the exception of the slide, there are currently no clear E&S or stabilization-related issues associated with the site. Big Dog is currently preparing all of the wells on this site to be placed into production. A contractor hired by Big Dog was working on establishing new barbed wire fencing around the location when this inspection was conducted. Some production equipment, including 3 GPU's are being staged on the site. The slip on the cut surface above the location was discussed with the contractor. Containment under the GPU's was also discussed, as well as updated well tags.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
Violation ID: 972624
Permit API: 015-23503
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Monroe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/12/2022
Comments: Weather was 55¿ and sunny. There were no Chesapeake representatives on location at time of inspection. Well was in production. Well had digital pressure monitoring equipment attached reading 960 PSI on the well head. Well had 3 annulus vents plumbed to surface with digital pressure monitoring equipment attached. The 20" X 13 3/8" annulus vent read -3 PSI, the 13 3/8" X 9 5/8" annulus vent read 0 PSI and the 9 5/8" X 5 1/2" annulus vent read 0 PSI. The 20" X 13 3/8" annulus vent was open to atmosphere and 100% LEL and 72% methane was detected. The 13 3/8" X 9 5/8" and 9 5/8" X 5 1/2" annulus vents were plumbed to a production tank. As a result, these annular spaces could not be monitored with the gas meter during this inspection. 0% combustible gas was detected anywhere around the well at time of inspection.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8269639
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/01/2026
Comments: On 04/01/2026 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County. The weather was 55 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last 24 hours. I arrived at 0930 hours. The DEP met with Repsol representative Ralph Babcock onsite. We traveled the area of the impact together. There are still two 24/7 water trucks onsite actively recovering fluids. Fluids above the release point were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~1080 us/cm (1 us/cm = 0.001 mS/cm) (photo #2). Those fluids continued traveling through the stormwater ditch into the active sumps (photo #3 and 4). They have excavated up to feet of material was removed from the ditch. The EC of fluids within the sump #1 and 2 was ~1.2 mS/cm. At that time Repsol instructed the truck operator to move his hoses below the sumps to start recovering those fluids which measured ~3.10 mS/cm (photo #5). The EC of the fluids that were directly entering the stormwater basin were ~540 us/cm. The stormwater basin has a containment in place (photo #7). Fluids were being recovered on top of and below the containment. ~60 barrels had been recovered today from the stormwater basin and sump #3. The EC of the fluids directly downgrade of the stormwater basin outlet and before sump #3 was ~5.1 mS/cm. The EC of fluids located below sump #3 was ~6.38 mS/cm. Brow/black vegetation was observed in that area (photo #11 and 12). We traveled downstream and the EC of the fluids were ~1.4 mS/cm. A spring intercepted the path of the flow from above grade. The EC of the fluids downstream of the spring was ~1.2-1.4 mS/cm. The EC of the marsh area was ~1.5 mS/cm. The EC of the UNT to Rockwell Creek upstream of the impacts was 25.3 us/cm (0.0253 mS/cm). Fluids entering UNT to Rockwell Creek at the upper confluence were field measured for EC at 2.4-2.7mS/cm (photo #18). From the upper confluence of the impact to the wetland inflow EC was 185.9- 225 us/cm (0.1859 -0.225 mS/cm) (photo #19). The EC of fluids from the UNT Rockwell Creek downstream impact was 379 us/cm.Repsol stated the stimulation activities for API #015-23994, 23995, 23996, 23997 and 23998 are scheduled to begin on 04/16/2026. Violations against API #015-23994 remain open at this time. I departed at 1100 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator Chief Oil &Amp; Gas Llc
Violation Type Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date 2013-07-26
Violation Code 402CSL - Failure to adopt pollution prevention measures required or prescribed by DEP by handling materials that create a danger of pollution.
Violation ID 674226
Permit API 115-21214
Unconventional Y
County Susquehanna
Municipality Springville Twp
Inspection Type Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date 2013-07-26
Comments Arrived at the site at 13:45 in response to a mineral oil spill. Patterson UTI Drilling Rig #257 is the active drilling rig on location currently driling the 3H well at (371) feet. Rich Adams, Environemtal Compliance Manager of Chief Oil and Gas, contacted the Department on 7/26/13 to report a release of an estimated (20) barrels of oil to secondary containment that occurred in the mid-morning of 7-25-13. The Marcellus incident report indicates the spill occurred as a result of a valve left open on a tank. A hole was found in the secondary containment and the plastic pad cover under the containment. An estimated (84) gallons impacted the surface of the ground on the Well Pad and (18) barrels of the mineral were recovered. A vacuum truck was immediately dispatched to the site to gather oil on standing water under the plastic. The excavation commenced down to clean soil on the Well Pad and the spilled material did not leave the Well Pad. A full spill cleanup report is pending from the company.

Comments: A discharge of production fluids is evident at the Loomis Lease tank battery. Elevated specific conductance in soils was observed beneath one of the stock tank's drain valves within the secondary containment area as well as throughout a swath of stressed and dead vegetation downslope of the Loomis Lease tank battery. Brian Ayers (WQSS-DEP) and I (Mat Haemer WQS-DEP) were present for this inspection.Evidence of a concentrated flow of fluids was observed just beyond the secondary containment diking. Bare soils outside of containment were observed to have been eroded in a manner consistent with the channelized flow of a large volume of fluid. Observations of elevated specific conductance in soils within the road ditch continued to a culvert nearby to the Loomis Lease Loomis 3 OG well. Standing water at the outflow of this culvert was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 1,300 micro Siemens per centimeter. Elevated soil conductivity readings in excess of 1,000 micro Siemens per centimeter continued for approximately 100 feet from the outfall of the culvert.The total observed path of stressed/dead vegetation and elevated conductivity readings was approximately 750 feet in length and up to 30 feet in width. Because the volume of this release exceeds the 1 bbl threshold, the use of either the Act 2 or Alternative Remediation Process is required.It is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners provide the Department with receipts documenting the proper disposal of brine resulting from producing the Loomis Lease.

Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of produced fluid. The release occurred at the frac tanks near the wells just to the northwest of the wells. At the time of inspection, the quantity of released produced fluid was unknown but was reported to be at least 1 barrel. I met onsite with Mike Deming, Expand. There were two sets of containment, each approximately 70' long by 55' wide. The staining appeared to be concentrated near the front-center of the tanks and between the two sets of containment for about half the length of the tanks. There were some holes identified in the offload area of the secondary containment shown in Photo 3. Soil conductivity was checked using a Groline soil conductivity meter. The damp areas/fluid were greater than 4.00 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm) which is the upper limit of the conductivity meter. Expand indicated that the conductivity of a few puddles in these areas was around 21 mS/cm, having used a YSI meter. There were no other puddles on the pad surface or seeps found between the pad and the infiltration basins. The soil conductivity below the pad and in the basins ranged between 0.05 mS/cm and 0.68 mS/cm.The set of tanks in the foreground of Photo 1 are going to be cleaned and removed in order to pull the containment. Some of the tanks in the background of Photo 1 will also be removed and the containment lifted as much as possible to facilitate a full assessment and remediation of the impacted area. The remediation is tentatively scheduled to begin 7/9/25.Per a discussion with Mike Deming, the site will be remediated under Act 2 requirements. The result of this inspection is Violations noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). There are also outstanding violations for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a) due to a release documented in inspection 3981577 from 5/20/25 and inspection 3982600 from 5/22/25. The release detailed in those inspections is also undergoing Act 2 remediation. The violations may be closed after the completion of Act 2 remediation.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Dorso Lp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: New Stanton Boro
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 2020-02-14
Comments: This inspection is being conducted in response to a notification received by the Department from the operator of plugging being conducted at this site. Assisting with this inspection is WQS Eric Norman. Conditions on site are cloudy, light snow on the ground, and approximately 30 degrees. The access road appears rutted with several locations that have standing water present. One such location (Photo 1-3) has what appears to be an outfall basin where two streams meet and then pass under the access road via a culvert heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. It appears that at this location some sediment laden water may have left the road in the vicinity of the hay bales (Photo 1), went down slope and discharged into this basin. At the time of this inspection it does not appear to be currently ongoing. The straw bale barriers at this location do not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. A second location (Photo's 4-7) is actively discharging sediment laden water into WOTC. The water appears to be pooling at a low point on the access road, spilling into a ditch which is conveying through a culvert pipe underneath the access road into a stream heading in the direction of Trib 37653 of Sewickley Creek. A straw bale barrier at this location does not appear to have been installed correctly (See Standard Detail 4-13 in the E&S Manual 363-2134-008, pg. 90). The bales do not appear to have been staked, trenched, or back fill applied. This appears to have allowed sediment laden stormwater to go around the bales and enter WOTC. The Department recommends that the operator immediately address this deficiency in order to prevent any further impacts to WOTC. The well appears plugged with a monument present with the API number affixed. There is no machinery present on the site. The site does not appear to have been temporarily stabilized and no down slope E&S controls are present. There does not appear to be an E&S Plan on site. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate steps to temporarily stabilize the site to prevent the potential for accelerated erosion or sedimentation. The Department recommends that the operator have E&S Plans prepared by a person trained and experienced in E&S Control methods and techniques applicable to the size and scope of the project and that those plans be on site during all phases of the earth disturbance activity. The Department also recommends that the operator installs downslope controls to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring at the site. An operator representative was spoken to via phone about the conditions on site. Mr. Wagner stated that no E&S Plans had been developed for this project and due to the weather conditions, no efforts were made to stabilize the site against accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Based on this inspection violations are being issued to the operator. The Department requests a timeline and action plan for abating the discharge and possible discharges identified in this inspection. Further violations may be issued based on responses received from the operator.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 1/13/2026
Comments: On 01/13/2026, an incident inspection was conducted following notification of a spill that occurred on 01/02/2026 at the NV48 Well Site. The Department first received notification of the spill 01/09/2026 from CNX (CTS 39456). I was accompanied by Ralph Barb (PA DEP), Melissa Cherry of Penn E and R, SPSI, and CNX representative Joe Fletcher.Per CNX, spill was said to have been reported to the Departments emergency hotline on 01/02/2026 via the 1 (800) 541-2050 phone number, however the Department did not have a history of a notification. Justin Ruth of CNX submitted a call log of the call, which occurred at 5:48 PM on 01/02/2026.On 01/09/2026, Chad Eisenman of CNX notified the Department of the spill; it was reported that 5 bbls of combined brine and freshwater released onto the pad at the NV48 Well Site on 01/02/2026. The spill was identified at approximately 3:48 PM and reported to the hotline at approximately 5:58 PM. Soil and gravel were impacted on the pad, the spill was contained to the pad, and no Waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. CNX is utilizing the alternative spill remediation standards under Act 2.The following was observed during inspection:The spill originated from two produced water tanks (brine) on containment, and a freshwater tank. Produced fluid back-fed into the freshwater tank, and the combined fluids released out of the freshwater tank onto the pad. 5 barrels (bbls) were released (Photo 1).The majority of the impacted material on the pad has been remediated. The impacted area furthest from the tanks yielded conductivity readings ranging from 98.6 - 551 S/cm (Photos 2-6).The surface material was scraped and removed, and trenches/sumps were dug. Conductivity readings within the trenches yielded readings ranging from 1148 S/cm - 3.46 mS/cm (Photos 7-11).Conductivity readings closer to the tanks and the front section of the impacted area ranged from 1469 S/cm - 7.41 mS/cm (Photos 12-18).The area was still in the process of remediation; however it was anticipated to be done the day of the Departments inspection (Photos 19-21).A background conductivity reading was obtained near the edge of the pad. The reading was 655 S/cm (Photos 22, 23).It was noted on site that the roll off dumpster was the fifth one to be used for the waste. I observed incorrect labeling on the roll off (Photo 24).The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan and the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan were both at the site entrance (Photo 25).Due to the release of production fluid combined with freshwater over a barrel, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

Comments: On 3/22/23 an incident inspection of the Veres Well Pad was conducted in response to a report of a spill reported to the Department on 3/22/23 (CTS: 370763).Background:On 3/22/23 I spoke to Keith Eighmey of Greylock to regarding a missed call from him the previous evening (3/21/23). Mr. Eighmey informed me that he had reported a spill to the Department hotline. The spill had occurred on the Veres Well Pad. According to Mr. Eighmey, an estimated 30 gallons of brine were released into an earthen containment berm. Greylock was in the process of removing the old tanks at the site to install new tanks with approved secondary containment. Two incidents resulted in the release. A small volume of brine mixed with sand and residual material was released when a manhole cover on the back of a tank was unbolted. Containment was being used at the time, but the volume of fluid mixed with the sediment overflowed out of the containment. Additionally, a vacuum truck was being used to draw down the tanks. The tank on the back of the truck was overfilled. When the suction was turned off, the excess fluid escaped back through the hose and onto the pad. I informed Mr. Eighmey that I would be coming out for a site inspection later the same day (3/22/23).The following was observed during the site inspection:-An Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance (Photo #1).-A crew was present excavating the spill area (Photo #2). According to Mr. Eighmey, they initially used ground liner containment yesterday to begin remediation efforts (Photo #3). However, Greylock has since acquired roll-off boxes and will transfer the waste that is currently on the liner into the boxes (Photo #4). -The old tanks were present and will be removed from the site (Photos #3 and #5-6).-A vacuum truck was present at the site (Photo #7).-Elevated conductivity was observed in pooled water that was slowly dripping from the sidecut of the excavated area (Photo #10).-Elevated conductivity was observed in a saturated layer of substrate below the gravel (Photos #8-9).-Elevated conductivity was not observed in the bottom of the excavated area (Photo #11). -No elevated conductivity was observed in the PCSM berms downslope of the release (Photos #12-13 and #17).-No elevated conductivity was observed at the drain outlet downslope of the release (Photos #15-16 and #17).According to Mr. Eighmey, they plan to continue excavation, install lined sump to monitor for the next few days to ensure full remediation. Additionally, Mr. Eighmey stated that Greylock is planning to follow 78a66(c)1 policy however, if further remediation efforts indicate that the release volume is greater than the initial estimate they will notify the Department and proceed with Act 2 procedures. Violations of 91.34(a), 78a57(a), 78a54, and SWMA 301 are being issued for the release.

Report Details

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 991891
Permit API: 053-27474
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/17/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a third party report of crude oil accumulated outside of the tank battery located at this well site.Upon my arrival, I observed a steel stock tank within an earthen containment located behind a conventional well that is equipped with a pump jack. There are currently no appreciable accumulations evident inside of the containment. There is evidence of recent earth disturbance along the western wall of the earthen containment. Just beyond the west/southwest corner of the tank battery, aged crude oil is present over an approximate 50' path of varying widths across the forest floor. At this time, there is no active discharge and the released product appears to have remained within an isolated swale/low lying area. It appears that the source of the product originates from the vicinity of the tank battery, however with the well being in close proximity, the source of the released crude oil is currently unclear. No watercourses appear to have been impacted by this release.Stuart Morris of Pennhills was contacted after this inspection and I relayed my findings to him. Stuart was not aware of any releases from the tank battery, but he did state that the well was recently serviced. Pennhills intends to investigate the matter and begin cleanup operations.It is requested that Pennhills provide an explanation of what occurred on the well site to result in the crude oil release in their response to the Notice of Violation (NOV) that is included in this inspection report. Please note other information that is requested in the NOV.Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate the status of cleanup efforts and to review or further investigate the source of the release.

Comments: On August 28, 2026, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident response inspection at the Range Resources Laurel Hill Well Pad B access road. While the DEP was conducting an inspection of the reported release of reuse water outside of containment onto the slope of the well pad, a water truck delivering the reuse water to the WMGR123 proceeded to drive off the access road causing the truck to roll over. Drip pans and a sheet of containment were placed under the truck where diesel fuel could be seen dripping from the exterior of the truck. The storage tank on the truck did not appear to have lost any of its contents. A Range Resources contractor was able to off load half of the truck's storage tank contents into an empty water truck. Once the water truck was righted, the DEP and Range Resources Kirby Steck were able to observe if the contents of the storage tank on the truck were released. The DEP and Range Resources probed the area of the truck rollover with soil conductivity meters and did not measure any areas with elevated soil conductivity. Before the contractor was able to get the drip pans and containment under the trucks cab, approximately 5 gallons of diesel fuel leaked onto the vegetated area next to the access road. Range Resources Kirby Steck said once the contractor was finished excavating the area of impact from the filter pod release onto the well,pad slope, they would begin excavating the impacted soil from the truck rollover.Violations of the Clean Stream Law 402(b) and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted due to the spilling of diesel fuel outside of containment onto the ground.

Comments: On 8/22/2024 at 1100 hrs., Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) representative John Rogers conducted an Incident - Response to Accident or Event Inspection (INCDT) of the Seneca Resources - Bauer 849 well pad located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. Complaint Id: 383218. It was 66 and partly cloudy when I arrived at the site.When I arrived at the site, I met Seneca's company man, Adam Pierce. Adam explained current operations as follows: A Nextier frac fleet is on site performing stimulation operations on seven recently drilled wells. The crew is currently zippering between 64HU, 66HU and 67HU wells with the other four wells already completed. Adam expects the crew to be done fracking the wells by August 24, 2024.Adam showed me where the spill event occurred. Tighe Truman joined us during the inspection. A water hauling truck like the one shown in pictures 3, 4 and 5 was backed up to the frac tanks located along the south edge of the pad. The truck driver was running the on-board air pump to provide air pressure to help push the liquids out of the tank. While the water truck was pressuring up, a pop-off valve valve that was connected to the top hatch on the front of the tank released pressure and released an estimated 20 gallons of produced water from the tank, the liquids impacting the ground under the truck and flowing a short distance east. The truck driver was at the controls on the side of the truck and immediately stopped pressuring the truck. Normally the pop-off valve should be above the fluid level but the front wheels of the truck were parked in a small depression that allowed the level of fluid to be above the pop-off connection. Discussing this incident with Adam and Tighe, the normal operating pressure is unknown and the pressure that the pop-off released at is unknown. It was unknown at the time of this inspection if the valve failed and opened below the designed relief pressure or if the driver allowed the pressure in the tank to exceed the designed pop-off relief pressure. Adam did say that it was a new driver and believes that the driver did not open the discharge valve on the truck before applying pressure. Adam commented that with the small air pocket of a fully loaded truck, it would only take a short amount of time to build up pressure. The area of the release is shown in pictures 3 and 6. The surface of the area has been scraped and new gravel has been installed. The scraped material was placed into a rolloff dumpster that, due to a previous spill, was already stationed at the site. The dumpster is lined and staged in secondary containment. Water in the truck offloading catch basin field tested at 11.06 mS conductance. Water in the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 19.49 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance liquids with Adam who said that he would have employees continue cleaning out the containments.The release of well-bore fluids to the unprotected pad surface constitutes violations of these three regulations; SWMA 301, CSL 402(b) and 25 PA Code 78a.56. The spill had been cleaned up, resulting in VIOICs (Violation noted and Immediately Corrected).The DEP recommends the following: 1. Discuss with the trucking company the need to inspect the equipment involved with this incident to ensure it is in serviceable condition. The pop-off valve should be examined to determine if it operated correctly or failed. Remove/repair equipment as necessary.2. Ensure personnel are trained on the safe and proper procedure for offloading fluids from tanker trucks.3. Screen the area impacted by the release of well-bore fluids for additional contamination and continue with cleanup as necessary.4. Continue to remove the elevated conductance fluid from the frac tank secondary containment and the unloading catch basin. Train personnel on proper procedures to prevent releasing the elevated conductance fluids into the containments. I left the site at 1230 hours.

Adam explained current operations as follows: A Nextier frac fleet is on site performing stimulation operations on seven recently drilled wells. The crew is currently zippering between 64HU, 66HU and 67HU wells with the other four wells already completed. Adam expects the crew to be done fracking the wells by August 24, 2024.Adam showed me where the spill event occurred. Tighe Truman joined us during the inspection. A water hauling truck like the one shown in pictures 3, 4 and 5 was backed up to the frac tanks located along the south edge of the pad. The truck driver was running the on-board air pump to provide air pressure to help push the liquids out of the tank. While the water truck was pressuring up, a pop-off valve valve that was connected to the top hatch on the front of the tank released pressure and released an estimated 20 gallons of produced water from the tank, the liquids impacting the ground under the truck and flowing a short distance east. The truck driver was at the controls on the side of the truck and immediately stopped pressuring the truck. Normally the pop-off valve should be above the fluid level but the front wheels of the truck were parked in a small depression that allowed the level of fluid to be above the pop-off connection. Discussing this incident with Adam and Tighe, the normal operating pressure is unknown and the pressure that the pop-off released at is unknown. It was unknown at the time of this inspection if the valve failed and opened below the designed relief pressure or if the driver allowed the pressure in the tank to exceed the designed pop-off relief pressure. Adam did say that it was a new driver and believes that the driver did not open the discharge valve on the truck before applying pressure. Adam commented that with the small air pocket of a fully loaded truck, it would only take a short amount of time to build up pressure. The area of the release is shown in pictures 3 and 6. The surface of the area has been scraped and new gravel has been installed. The scraped material was placed into a rolloff dumpster that, due to a previous spill, was already stationed at the site. The dumpster is lined and staged in secondary containment. Water in the truck offloading catch basin field tested at 11.06 mS conductance. Water in the frac tank secondary containment field tested at 19.49 mS conductance. I discussed the elevated conductance liquids with Adam who said that he would have employees continue cleaning out the containments.The release of well-bore fluids to the unprotected pad surface constitutes violations of these three regulations; SWMA 301, CSL 402(b) and 25 PA Code 78a.56. The spill had been cleaned up, resulting in VIOICs (Violation noted and Immediately Corrected).The DEP recommends the following: 1. Discuss with the trucking company the need to inspect the equipment involved with this incident to ensure it is in serviceable condition. The pop-off valve should be examined to determine if it operated correctly or failed. Remove/repair equipment as necessary.2. Ensure personnel are trained on the safe and proper procedure for offloading fluids from tanker trucks.3. Screen the area impacted by the release of well-bore fluids for additional contamination and continue with cleanup as necessary.4. Continue to remove the elevated conductance fluid from the frac tank secondary containment and the unloading catch basin. Train personnel on proper procedures to prevent releasing the elevated conductance fluids into the containments. I left the site at 1230 hours.

Comments: On April 14, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The hole in the well pad trench liner near the northwest stormwater vault has been fixed. Two patches have been added to the trench liner. There was about 8 inches of water in northwest stormwater vault. About 12 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in either vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. There has been no pad surface remediation completed. The DEP screened the five seeps and three stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 20.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 26.4. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 190 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 274 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 32.6 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 40.1 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 169.4 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.8 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. Infiltration berm 1 along the access road that had a section erode observed on February 18, 2022 has been filled in and compost filter sock has been added near the berm. The other four infiltration berms with erosion noted in Inspection Report 3324293 have been filled in. The infiltration berms along the access road have not been seeded or temporarily stabilized. It appears that earth work on the infiltration berms along the access road has been completed. The DEP recommend seeding and temporarily stabilizing the infiltration berms according to ¿102.22(b). This will help with preventing another situation of sediment discharging outside of the LOD and help prevent accelerated erosion of bare earth. Infiltration berms 1, 2, 6, 7, and 9 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Comments: This inspection was performed in response to a report, by the Operator, of a small release of crude oil along Irvine Run, in Brokenstraw Township, Warren County, PA. This is the second release to have occurred in association with this well this year. Please reference inspection ID#: 2870841. I was contacted by Rick Engelbert with Irvine Run Resources on September 13, 2019 to report the release of an unknown volume of crude oil to the ground along Irvine Run. The spill was reported to have been contained and was actively being cleaned up. A site visit was arranged for September 16, 2019. Legree 30, (37-123-26419): I met with Rick Engelbert on site at approximately 10:30 on September 16, 2019 to conduct an site investigation. Rick indicated that the well was pumped on August 31, 2019. A strong odor was noticed near the well on September 1st. A small amount of oil was found to have been seeping from the ground surface at the base of a hill side some ways below the well location;(At a similar elevation as the spill that occurred in April but further down on Irvine Run). A syphon dam was constructed below the area that was seeping oil. Absorbent materials were applied periodically to absorb the oil. A boom and some straw bails were placed in the stream channel of Irvine Run as a precautionary measure. Very little oil was believed to have made it into the stream. A leak test was performed on the buried lead line system that services the well. A small hole was found in a portion of the line near the well. The excavation exposing the line was still open while I was on site. All of the contaminated soil appeared to have been removed from the hole. Similar to the excavation created to expose the last leak associated with this well, the soil that was excavated didn't seem to have much oil contamination. Heavy rain in the last week apparently caused the volume of oil draining from the seep to increase. It was at this point that Rick contacted me to report the spill. Approximately ten gallons of oil is reported to have been gather up. I noticed a slight emulsion on the surface of the water behind the syphon dam while I was on site. The spill appears to be getting managed appropriately at this point. The operator indicated the absorbent materials will continue to be changed as needed. It has been advised to the operator that recoverable waste materials, including the contaminated soil that was excavated around the leak, be collected and disposed of at a land fill. A receipt of disposal should be sent to the Warren District Office upon disposal. The clean up progress will continue to be monitored with future inspections.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8235126
Permit API: 015-23893
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/27/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Broadleaf Holdings" Marcellus well site. Tory Rogers called the DEP on Friday morning May 23, 2025 to report a release of approximately 9 gallons of diesel based drilling mud released from a flare stack to the pad surface that morning. I met with Tory Rogers, Jim Brown, Megan DePue (all 3 Repsol), and Scotty Brown (DEP, OGI) on site. While drilling a future Marcellus Shale well there was a control issue, so they lit the flare stack to burn off natural gas incurred. Some drilling mud blew out of the flare stack, estimated at 7 gallons onto pad containment, and 9 gallons on the pad surface. Rogers showed us where the flare stack released drilling mud. Resource Environmental directed excavation to remove pad material the drilling mud impacted, which was approximately a 10'X60' area. They completed the cleanup around 1600 hrs the same day the release occurred. The material is in 2 dumpsters on the NE corner of the pad. I got a 1.5 ppm reading with a 10.6 eV MiniRae photoionization detector (PID) from the removed pad material, and a 0.0 ppm PID reading from the remediated pad surface, which indicates the cleanup sufficiently removed the impacted pad material. Drill cuttings in a dumpster near the drill rig gave a 135.7 ppm reading. Violations cited to the 015-23893 drilling permit are considered immediately corrected.Rogers explained they increased the density of the drill mud from 12.8 lbs/gal to 13.5 lbs/gal to provide more well control.Repsol laid the containment on this pad on February 26 thru March 3, 2025. Felt liner (130 mil thickness) went down first, then wood/steel mats. Fine gravel is used to fill gaps between the mats.Precision Drilling 110 started drilling 4 new Marcellus wells at this site on April 1 2025, and expect to finish drilling around June 10, 2025. There are also 4 existing Marcellus wells here. They drill on water based mud for the vertical section, then switch to diesel based mud for the kickoff (curve) and horizontal section.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity (EC) of 0.68-1.7 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.62FJLP

Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of about 122 barrels of produced water.Chesapeake suspects the produced water tank onsite was struck by lightning. The produced water leaked from the bottom of the tank and was contained on the pad. The impacted area is in the southeast corner of the pad between the GPUs and containment berm. There were 2 areas of concentrated excavation but the total impacted area is expected to be less than approximately 30'x70' and about 1' deep.Conductivity measurements were performed to determine the perimeter of the impacted area and guide further excavation. At the time of inspection the area was continuing to be excavated and about 5 tri-axle loads of soil had already been removed and placed on secondary containment. The damaged tank has already been removed.Creston Environmental will collect confirmation samples to verify that the impacted area has been fully remediated. A temporary storage tank will be brought to the site to replace the damaged tank. It will be placed in front of the GPUs to keep access to the impacted area open.Violations have been cited for a release of produced water to the pad surface and Chesapeake will pursue remediation under Act 2 requirements.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT PROD CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/20/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8245730
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/20/2025
Comments: On August 20, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of EQT's Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4014690 and violations issued for a 1-3 barrel release of a production fluid, frack chemical and fresh water mixture.The findings are as follows:At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Act 9 sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that had a different Operator's information posted on it. The Department recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the perimeters of the well site were observed to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues.At the time of this inspection, there appeared to be rain water puddles in the area of the previous release and scraping of contaminated gravel. The Department did not observe a sheen in any puddles of apparent rainwater in the release area. The Department did not observe the trench previously observed to be bordering the secondary containment in the release area during IR 4014690. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the release area and collected the following soil conductivity readings: 0.75mS, 0.48mS, and 0.44mS . These readings were found to be comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.67mS.Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding at thus time pending the Act 2 Final report submittal, receipt, review, and approval by the Department's Environmental Cleanup and Brownfield Program.
